holidays.name: National Good Neighbor Day
holidays.description: A day to wave, bring over a plate of cookies, or finally return that ladder you borrowed in 2019. It celebrates the people next door and encourages communities to get friendlier.
holidays.origin: Created by Becky Mullins of Lakeview, Arkansas, who lobbied for years to have a day honoring neighbors. President Jimmy Carter issued a proclamation recognizing it in 1978, and the day is traditionally observed on the fourth Sunday of September, though September 28 is widely cited in unofficial calendars.
holidays.funFact: Becky Mullins reportedly started her campaign in the early 1970s and kept at it for years before a presidential proclamation made the day official.

holidays.name: National Drink Participation Day
holidays.description: A cheeky unofficial day inviting people to raise a glass, with the emphasis on participation, so a refreshing glass of water, lemonade, or your beverage of choice absolutely counts.
holidays.origin: This is one of those internet-era unofficial observances that spread through holiday calendars and social media, built around the simple idea of joining in on a toast with friends.
holidays.funFact: Hydration experts everywhere approve, since a plain glass of water technically qualifies as participating.

holidays.name: World Rabies Day
holidays.description: A serious but important awareness day that rallies the world to prevent rabies through vaccinations, education, and responsible pet care. It reminds us that this ancient disease is almost entirely preventable.
holidays.origin: Launched in 2007 by the Global Alliance for Rabies Control, with support from the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. It is held on September 28 to mark the death anniversary of Louis Pasteur, who developed the first rabies vaccine.
holidays.funFact: Louis Pasteur and his colleagues first tested their rabies vaccine on a human in 1885, when a nine-year-old boy named Joseph Meister was bitten by a rabid dog and survived.

holidays.name: National Strawberry Cream Pie Day
holidays.description: A dessert holiday dedicated to a dreamy slice of fluffy cream, juicy strawberries, and flaky crust, ideal for anyone who thinks fruit is better when buried under whipped topping.
holidays.origin: Like many food days, it grew from the dessert-loving corners of the internet and holiday calendars, with no single known founder, and it fits neatly into the early autumn strawberry season in some regions.
holidays.funFact: Strawberries are the only fruit with seeds on the outside, averaging around 200 seeds per berry.

holidays.name: International Day for Universal Access to Information
holidays.description: A day championing the idea that everyone should be able to find, read, and share public information, from government records to your library's weirdest dusty book.
holidays.origin: The United Nations General Assembly and UNESCO proclaimed it in 2019, building on a day originally recognized by UNESCO's General Conference in 2015, to promote transparency and the public's right to know.
holidays.funFact: Sweden passed one of the world's first freedom of information laws back in 1766.
